Public Comment: The public is encouraged to address the Housing Authority on any matter listed on the agenda or on any other matter
within its jurisdiction subject to the rules of decorum described in Section 2.08.020 of the Norwalk Municipal Code. If you wish to address
the Housing Authority, please complete the card that is provided at the rear entrance to Council Chambers and hand the card to the
Sergeant at Arms. The Housing Authority will hear public comment on items listed on the agenda during discussion of the matter and
prior to a vote. The Housing Authority will hear public comment on matters not listed on the agenda during the Oral Communications
period.

Pursuant to provisions of the Brown Act, no action may be taken on a matter unless it is listed on the agenda, or unless certain emergency
or special circumstances exist. The Housing Authority may direct staff to investigate and/or schedule certain matters for consideration
at a future Housing Authority meeting.

Please adhere to the following procedures when addressing the Housing Authority:
   Comments should be limited to 3 minutes or less.
   Comments should be directed to the Housing Authority as a whole and not directed to individual Commissioners.

Americans with Disabilities Act: In compliance with the ADA, if you need special assistance to participate in a City meeting or other
services offered by this City, please contact the City Clerk’s office, (562) 929-5720. Assisted listening devices are available at this
meeting. Ask the City Clerk if you desire to use this device. Upon request, the agenda and documents in the agenda packet can be
made available in appropriate alternative formats to persons with a disability. Notification of at least 48 hours prior to the meeting or time
when services are needed will assist the City staff in assuring that reasonable arrangements can be made to provide accessibility to the
meeting or service.

Note: Any writings and/or documents provided to a majority of the Housing Authority regarding any item on this agenda after it has been
posted will also be made available for public inspection.

Writings and/or documents are available for inspection in the City Clerk’s Department, City Hall, 12700 Norwalk Boulevard during regular
business hours, 8:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m., Monday – Thursday and 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., every other Friday; telephone (562) 929-5720.
You may also contact the City Clerk via e-mail at recordsrequests@norwalkca.gov.

SUBJECT:  HOUSING ASSISTANCE PAYMENTS PROGRAM – APPROVE
  WARRANT RUN SEPTEMBER 15, 2019 – OCTOBER 1, 2019

Background:

The Housing Authority made payments during the period of September 15, 2019 through
October 1, 2019 for a grand total $617,762.45.

Fiscal Impact: N/A

Citizens Advised: N/A

Strategic Action Plan Implementation: N/A

Recommended Action:

Staff recommends the Housing Authority approve Check Nos. 66804 & 213548 - 213551
reported on September 15, 2019 for a total of $7,377.00 and Check Nos. 66805 - 66828
& 213552 - 213707 reported on October 1, 2019 for a total of $610,385.45.

Attachments:

1. Check Summary Information Sheet
2. Check Summary
   ATTACHMENT 1
  Housing Authority
  Check Summary Information Sheet

The warrants in the Housing Authority agenda report are for housing assistance payments
made under the Section 8 Housing Choice Voucher program. The payee has a choice of
receiving the housing assistance payment via direct deposit, which is an electronic fund
transfer made directly to the payee’s bank account, or by paper check.

In the check summary report, the direct deposits are listed first as direct deposits, and then
the checks follow. Each direct deposit and paper check represents payment for 1 to 20
tenants depending upon the number of Section 8 tenants the payee has.

The payee is the property owner or designated management company. The property owner
or manager may be a corporation, partnership, trust, or individual. The payee name is the
owner or manager’s legal business or individual name, which must match Internal Revenue
Service (IRS) records. Here are some common abbreviations used in business names:

LLC = Limited Liability Company

LP = Limited Partnership

DBA = “Doing Business As”

LTD = Limited

Checks made out to the City of Norwalk Housing Authority represent the Family Self
Sufficiency (FSS) escrow deposits. These checks are deposited into the Housing Authority’s
bank account where the funds earn interest and are kept in escrow until the FSS participant
successfully completes the program at which time they receive the balance of their account.

Norwalk Housing Investors, LP is the owner of Center Pointe Villas at 14100 San Antonio
and 11856 Orange. Payments are for Section 8 participants living in these buildings.

Payments to housing authorities, such as the Orange County Housing Authority and San
Bernardino County Housing, represent reimbursements for our participants who have
transferred to those jurisdictions under portability.

Please call Kristin Maithonis at ext. 5653 if you have any questions.

SUBJECT:  RESOLUTION NO. NHA-159 - AUTHORIZING THE FILING OF A GRANT
  APPLICATION TO THE UNITED STATES DEPARTMENT OF HOUSING
  AND URBAN DEVELOPMENT FOR THE FAMILY SELF-SUFFICIENCY
  PROGRAM AND AUTHORIZING THE EXECUTIVE DIRECTOR TO
  EXECUTE ANY REQUIRED GRANT AGREEMENTS

Background:

The Housing Authority currently administers a Family Self-Sufficiency (FSS) program with
the support of the Family Self-Sufficiency program grant received from the United States
Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD). The FSS program assists
Section 8 participants with identifying barriers to success and obtaining services to
become economically self-reliant. The FSS program grant is offered annually on a
competitive basis and only funds the salary and benefits of staff performing FSS program
functions. Staff involved in the FSS program provide ongoing case management to
participants and utilize local resources to reduce welfare dependency and increase
participants’ incomes.

On September 26, 2019, HUD announced the Notice of Funding Availability (NOFA) for
the FSS program renewal grant, and the application due date is October 28, 2019. HUD
has capped the maximum grant amount at $36,000. The cap is based upon the number
of FSS participants assisted by the Housing Authority during Calendar Year 2018. The
FSS program currently has 15 active participants and has had 50 graduates since the
program began in 1995.

Fiscal Impact: N/A

Citizens Advised: N/A

  WHEREAS, funds are being made available under the Consolidated
Appropriations Act, 2019 and United States Department of Housing and Urban
Development’s funding opportunity number FR-6300-N-04 for a Family Self-Sufficiency
(FSS) Program, not to exceed $36,000; and

  WHEREAS, the City of Norwalk Housing Authority, being established in
accordance with Section 34290 et.seq., of the California Health and Safety Code, is
administering a Family Self-Sufficiency Program under the Section 8 Housing Choice
Voucher Program; and

  WHEREAS, the City of Norwalk Housing Authority is also currently supporting
positions with funding previously received from HUD.

  NOW, THEREFORE, THE CITY OF NORWALK HOUSING AUTHORITY
HEREBY DETERMINES, FINDS, AND RESOLVES AS FOLLOWS:

  Section 1. That staff prepare a grant application and relevant documentation to
the United States Department of Housing and Urban Development to renew FSS grant
funding, not to exceed $36,000.

  Section 2. That the Executive Director or his designee is authorized to execute
and submit the grant application and documentation by the application deadline of
October 28, 2019.

  Section 3. That the Executive Director is authorized to execute any required
grant agreements.
